really: I really enjoyed the concert despite the terrible weather.
about: The lecture was about how cities cope with extreme heat.
simple: easy to understand or do; not complicated
He gave a simple explanation that even a child could understand.
question: /ˈkwestʃən/
n
a sentence asked to get information or express doubt
câu hỏi, vấn đề
Nobody could answer the teacher's difficult question about gravity.
query
inquiry
issue
who: used to ask about or refer to a person
The extra heat is dangerous for anyone who cannot afford to cool their home.
an: used before a word starting with a vowel sound to mean 'one'
She ordered an apple juice and a sandwich for lunch.
easier: The new software makes editing photos much easier.
crowded: full of people; having little empty space
The train was so crowded that several passengers had to stand.
feeds: The farm feeds several hundred families in the district.
thousands: a very large number of people or things, counted in units of a thousand
Thousands of workers gathered outside the factory to demand better pay.
good: of high quality, favourable, or beneficial
It was a good decision to leave early before the storm.
answer: a response given to a question or problem
Her answer to the interview question impressed every member of the panel.
will: used to express the future tense
A fact heard once looks, from the inside, like a fact that will never be needed again.
probably: almost certainly; likely to be true
He is probably still at work; his car is not in the driveway.
need: to require something because it is essential
Plants need sunlight and water in order to grow well.
room: a space within a building enclosed by walls
She rearranged the furniture to make the room feel larger.
both: the two of something, referring to two things together
Both students finished the exam well before the time limit.
